title: Wait For Free: A Consumption-Decelerating Promotion for Serialized Digital Media
authors: Jangwon Choi; Inyoung Chae; Fred M. Feinberg
year_in_article: 2024 (JMR 62(1), 2025 issue; copyright 2024; batch year 2022 is the submission year)
eligible_reason: Staggered binary adoption with never-treated controls: the platform applied 'wait for free' (WFF) to comics in waves; the estimation window covers the first 8 waves (35 WFF comics adopting between November 2018 and February 2019) against 765 never-promoted comics, weekly comic-level panel of 19 pre and 16 post weeks. Treatment = 1{c in WFF} x 1{t in postWFF_c}. Table 5 reports a version with no controls and no reweighting (free views 3.303 (.071); paid views .797 (.043)). BORDERLINE: comic and week intercepts are specified as two-way RANDOM effects estimated by REML (regularized), not fixed effects; the authors report in Web Appendix Table WA4 that a fixed-effects version gives near-identical estimates, and Web Appendix Table WB2 reports Callaway-Sant'Anna doubly robust estimates of the same design. I kept the two no-control/no-IPW columns as eligible because a TWFE counterpart is directly constructible; the lead should confirm that random-effects intercepts are acceptable. The other six Table 5 columns use time-varying non-WFF promotion controls and/or inverse-propensity weights and are recorded as ineligible.
design_notes: Equation 1: log(Y^F_ct + 1) = b0 + bF*1{c in WFF}*1{t in postWFF_c} + X_ct*gamma + alpha_c + alpha_t + e, alpha_c ~ N(0, s2_c), alpha_t ~ N(0, s2_t), REML; analogous for paid views Y^P. X_ct (when included) = log number of days in week t that comic c was under a discount promotion, and log days under a 'more free episodes' promotion (time-varying). IPW version weights comics by inverse estimated propensity (logit on six comic characteristics, Table 4). Sample: top 800 comics (35 WFF + 765 non-WFF), weekly, June 26, 2018-February 25, 2019, N = 27,463 comic-weeks. Table 6: Equation 1 re-estimated on views from user subgroups (paying/nonpaying, frequent/infrequent), IPW. Figure 4: WFF effect by week since adoption w = 1..16 (post-only indicators, IPW). Equations 2-3 and Figure 5: episode-week random-effects model with comic- and episode-level time trends, spillover similarity terms and controls (not a DiD spec). False-date pretrend test p = .164 (free), .200 (paid). Web Appendix WB2: PSM, CEM and Callaway-Sant'Anna.
estimators_reported: two-way random-effects DiD (REML), with and without time-varying promotion controls
main_or_robustness: main (comic-level DiD is the first of two analyses; the episode-level model drives the optimization)
modern_estimators_named: Callaway-Sant'Anna (2021) doubly robust, Web Appendix Table WB2

data_availability_statement: None found. User-level viewership data from an unnamed global online entertainment platform under a nondisclosure agreement (footnote 1). Submitted April 29, 2022, before JMR's July 2023 transparency policy.
screener_notes: Software inferred from the R package kofnGA used for the optimization; the mixed models are REML (likely lme4). Two judgment calls: (1) two-way random effects instead of fixed effects, kept as eligible because the authors show FE gives the same answer (Web Appendix WA4) and a TWFE counterpart is straightforward; (2) IPW columns treated as reweighting-based and excluded, though the protocol allows 'analysis weights'. Waves 9-12 (24 more comics) adopt after February 25, 2019 and are outside the window, so no control comic is treated within the sample. Wave dates are in Web Appendix Table WA1, not in the main text. Without a replication package the paper is priority 2.
